sections.h2: What This AI Video Ads Generator Makes
paras: It builds a short ad for a product you already list, such as this backpack. You can trim the clip before it goes on the store or into an ad account. The checks below are what you do before that.

Run this checklist on that file. Match the backpack to what you ship, then the words, the rights, and the rule on that site. A generated photo or video is a new picture made from your upload, not a duplicate of the source. A letter on a zipper pull can change, a buckle can move, an extra strap can appear, or a color can shift. Use the same check on a listing photo, a social post, and a paid ad.
sections.alt: Hands check the front pocket and zipper of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: How Do I Review a Finished Video Ad?
paras: Watch the file the way a shopper will, on a phone, with sound and captions on. Start from the first frame. Hold the real backpack next to the screen.

Check the file for the app where it will run. A TikTok ad and a Meta ad both need the backpack to match. Meta here means Facebook and Instagram. A tall file and a square file can still show the same backpack. For more finished examples, open UGC video ads. Then run the checks on the finished file.

sections.h2: How Do I Check AI Product Images?
paras: Hold the real backpack, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through color, shape, logos, parts, and size.

Compare the color in daylight, not only on a bright screen. Count the pockets, straps, and buckles. Read every letter on a label. If a hand is in the picture, the backpack should look the right size next to it. A styled scene might add a plant. Keep that extra item only when a shopper can tell it is not part of the order. Those scenes are made as [lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos). Count the parts there too.
sections.alt: Hands count pockets, buckles and straps on plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: What Is on an AI Video Review Checklist?
paras: Play the clip on your phone. Listen to the voice, and read the captions. Then go through it slowly. Watch the hands and the first frame of the backpack.

The script should name the backpack you ship. Do not mention a feature that is not for sale. Clips often go wrong while the product moves. A label can blur as it turns. Fingers can blend into a strap. A zipper can change shape halfway through. Count the fingers, and watch how they hold the item. The first frame often becomes the thumbnail shoppers see first. If one short moment looks wrong, trim it in the editor. If the problem runs through the whole clip, make a new version. Run this same check on a [product video](page:product-videos) before you post it.
sections.alt: Hands open the zipper and flap of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: How Do I Add the Price Before I Publish?
paras: Make the picture or the clip of the backpack first. Then add the price, the date, the code, and the headline yourself.

Do not ask the tool to paint those words into the image or the clip. Letters it draws are often wrong or messy. Captions can match the spoken line. You still type the price, the date, and the code yourself. Every character should match the product page. Before you post, match the price and the code to the store. Check that any end date is still ahead. If stray letters show on the backpack or a sign, remove that part of the picture or try again.
sections.alt: Plain black travel backpack centered on a white background.

sections.h2: What Do I Need to Own Before an AI Ad Goes Live?
paras: Upload only photos you took, or photos you have permission to use. Use only logos that belong to you, including the mark on this backpack.

If the photo comes from a supplier, your agreement with them must cover ads. A request built around another company's logo, or a celebrity, may be refused. The [Content Policy](/content) says what you can upload. For music, pick a track from the music library, or use one you already licensed for ads. The avatar and the voice you pick are for the ads you make. The tool says the line you approved, not a claim you never wrote.

sections.h2: When Do AI-Generated Content Labels Apply?
paras: Read the current rule on each site you post to. Several sites ask you to mark a realistic generated face or scene. That rule can change, so check it again before a big spend.

Keep two rules on every site. Do not show a generated face as a buyer or a reviewer. That includes [model photos for clothing](page:model-photos). Do not let a caption promise a health, skin, or weight result. Show how the backpack is used, and let the shopper decide.

sections.h2: Reasons to Make an AI Video Ad
paras: The script starts from your product page, or from the lines you type. If the backpack has one front pocket, the line does not say two. Run the checklist before you keep that opening.

The file comes out in a shape you pick before the job. Those shapes are listed on [pricing](page:pricing). 9:16 is a tall phone video. 1:1 is a square. 16:9 is a wide video. 4:3 and 3:4 are there too. 3:4 is a little taller than it is wide.
From one backpack photo you can ask for a calm try-on and a louder unboxing. Keep the version that fits the shop after you run this checklist.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Checked Video Ad
paras: A bag shop shows an AI avatar holding the backpack and naming the front pocket. A person then checks that pocket against the real bag before anyone posts it.
A gadget shop opens the box on a desk and confirms every part in the kit is the part that ships. They use the same slow pass you just used on the zipper.
A clothing shop shows the piece on an adult, then matches the neckline and the print to the sample before the file is saved.
A food shop sets the jar on a counter. The voice names the flavor printed on the lid, and no extra claim is added after the check.

sections.h2: Check the Product, Then Post the Ad
paras: Build the ad from a listing address, or from a short note you type. Then match the product, and type the price yourself. Use only photos, logos, and music you have the rights to use.
Send it to TikTok or Meta, or download it, only after those checks. If a shopper could feel misled, do not post that file.

faq.q: What does the video ads generator make?
faq.a: It makes a short ad from one product photo, a listing address, or lines you type. You still check the backpack, the words, and the rights before it goes live.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad with AI?
faq.a: Describe the one detail that must show, or paste the listing. Read the draft out loud. Save the file only after the checks are complete.

faq.q: When should a shop use an AI video ad?
faq.a: Use it when each product in a catalog needs its own clip. Skip it if you only need one filmed video of the founder.

faq.q: Do I pay before the first file?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo is 24 credits. A clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

faq.q: Can the file run as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. A paid plan is what lets the file run in an ad account, and the download has no watermark.

faq.q: Which sizes can I export, and where do they run?
faq.a: YouTube and a wide ad can take 16:9. A phone story wants 9:16. A square post wants 1:1. 4:3 and 3:4 are there too. TikTok and Meta are common places to run them, and you still check the spot before you spend.

faq.q: Can I create ads for multiple products at once?
faq.a: Yes. Send many products through a batch or the API. Each file shows its credit cost before it starts, and each one still needs this checklist.
Keep hiring when the ad needs a person buyers already know. Use this for the other products in the catalog, and check each file.

faq.q: Will TikTok or Meta block an AI ad?
faq.a: TikTok and Meta still accept a generated clip. They get stricter when the line sounds like a stranger already bought the product. Read their current ad rules before you put money on the file. The [Content Policy](/content) is ours.

faq.q: What should I check before posting an AI-made video?
faq.a: Watch it on your phone, from the first frame to the last. Check the product, the hands, the label, the voice, and the captions. Then check that any price you added matches the store.

faq.q: What if an extra object looks like it comes with the order?
faq.a: Do not use that version, or say clearly in the listing what is included. Decoration is fine only when a shopper would not expect it in the box.

faq.q: Can I ask the tool to draw my discount code?
faq.a: No. Add the code, the price, and the date yourself after you download, so the letters stay correct. Captions can follow what is spoken. They do not replace the price or the code.

faq.q: Can I use a supplier photo as the source?
faq.a: Only if your agreement with the supplier covers ads. Otherwise shoot your own photo of the item.

faq.q: What if one moment in the clip looks wrong?
faq.a: Trim that moment in the editor if it is brief. If the error runs through the clip, make a new version instead of posting it.
